newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault sees precedent in Thomson deal.
newsitem.headline: Dassault sees precedent in Thomson deal.

text.p: Officials at Dassault Aviation said the sale of state-owned Thomson SA to smaller, more profitable Lagardere should set a precedent for its planned merger with Aerospatiale, financial daily La Tribune reported on Monday.

"The Thomson-Matra affair offers us a precedent. A small, profitable private group can buy a big state-owned company that is financially fragile," the paper quoted an unnamed senior Dassault source as saying. "Why could Dassault not become the core shareholder of Aerospatiale?"
The government said in February it wanted to merge the two companies, and, under a plan due to be finalised by January 1, 1997, Aerospatiale would take the upper hand.
Dassault has said it opposes the plan.
But La Tribune reported that government officials would be in favour of Dassault management having a large role in managing the newly merged company.
